requirements.requirement: Kernel boots with audit=1 on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline /proc/cmdline lacked audit=1 (cmd-3cdb91a9a98e4f08, cmd-e7221c59af1d4ed1). After editing GRUB config and rebooting, post-reboot /proc/cmdline explicitly contains audit=1 (cmd-369d092dc509443e, cmd-8d111d10b6234839), directly confirming the running kernel booted with the parameter.

requirements.requirement: Setting persists across reboots (not just a one-time runtime change)
requirements.summary: Executor edited /etc/default/grub and discovered/fixed /etc/default/grub.d/50-cloudimg-settings.cfg, which would have silently overridden the first change (cmd-a8c7f676c2224b26, cmd-b592a291ce7a4ea8, cmd-41f72e9d64c349c8). update-grub was run and grub.cfg confirmed to contain audit=1 in the linux boot entries (cmd-df8a3e0ac91e437d, cmd-f2ba302d5d3c4922). A real reboot was then performed and verified via a changed boot_id (b185f188... -> b9f21be1...), and the post-reboot cmdline and running uptime/who -b confirm a fresh boot with audit=1 present, demonstrating actual persistence rather than just static config presence.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart boot identity/health, restart acknowledgement, distinct post-restart boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id b185f188-42be-40d1-84ea-f7c9a76f5c8d captured (cmd-4c6857ed9aff420b, cross-checked by global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity). Reboot was acknowledged via connection drop (cmd-9008fa5ca13e4bbb), node was unreachable during the transition (cmd-2b09a76da10b43df, cmd-95383fd7a60f41c1), then reachable again with a distinct boot_id b9f21be1-4c0d-493d-a714-2adee0effe6c (cmd-369d092dc509443e), matching the fixed global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity snapshot. No failed services, package-health issues, or listening-socket changes were introduced, and there is no cluster/data-service dependency for this single-node task.

overall_summary: The executor correctly identified that a cloud-image GRUB override (/etc/default/grub.d/50-cloudimg-settings.cfg) would have silently discarded a naive change to /etc/default/grub, fixed both files, regenerated grub.cfg, and performed a genuine reboot (verified via a changed boot_id) to confirm audit=1 is present on the running kernel's /proc/cmdline post-reboot. Both material outcomes (audit=1 active, and persistence across reboot) are directly demonstrated rather than merely inferred from static config. The independent restart-evidence protocol is also satisfied with matching before/after boot identities and no service or package regressions.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was observed; persistence across multiple future reboots is inferred from the corrected, generated grub.cfg content rather than repeatedly observed across several reboots.

auditd itself was not installed/active (auditctl not found, systemd auditd inactive) — the task only asked for the kernel boot parameter audit=1, not a functioning audit daemon, so this is not scored as a gap, but is noted for completeness.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (sed edits to /etc/default/grub and /etc/default/grub.d/50-cloudimg-settings.cfg, two update-grub runs, and the reboot) are directly tied to satisfying the task's persistence requirement; the second update-grub run was necessary after discovering the cloud-image override, not a wasted or unrelated mutation. The reboot itself is a required, bounded action for verifying cross-reboot persistence, not an extraneous mutation. Lifecycle diff shows only the expected boot-identity and ephemeral systemd-private /tmp directory changes tied to the reboot (executor_comparison), with no new failed services, listening sockets, or package-health regressions. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found.
